correctness.rationale: For two different interior fixed points, the maximal odds ratio R>1 yields x<=H_R(y). Strict concavity/Jensen equality and connectivity propagate equality to every vertex, then odd-cycle connectivity forces y constant, contradicting a nonneutral bias. For existence, positive Perron eigenvectors give strict lower and complementary upper barriers when both boundary multipliers exceed one. Strict Jensen on reciprocals plus Perron left eigenvectors proves both thresholds necessary. Convex/concave odds barriers prove attraction of all interior deterministic iterates and diminishing-step recursions. The stochastic conclusion invokes published Theorems 3 and 4 of arxiv:2308.09275, with three isolated equilibria. A two-node reciprocal-bias edge has a verified continuum of fixed points, proving sharpness. Standalone verify.py passed 162 rational/numerical assertions; numerical checks do not substitute for universal proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023 work expressly leaves arbitrary-network interior equilibrium uniqueness open. Resolving it gives a universal exact three-equilibrium classification, rigorous asymptotic identification rather than only set convergence, deterministic global attraction from all interior starts, and a sharp graph-theoretic failure boundary for reciprocal-bias bipartite networks. These are structurally motivated statements and are not small numerical variations or a special finite table.
